decisions.reason: As a new safety shoe line, it sits at the center of the firm's existing design, production, certification, and sales knowledge, so management is likely to keep refining rather than withdraw it.
A comfort insole is closely complementary to the firm's footwear business and foot-measurement capabilities, giving it strong absorptive capacity to improve fit and adoption.
A supportive insole draws on the firm's related know-how in protective footwear and customer-specific fit, so early market learning can be absorbed and translated into product improvements.
An ergonomic safety shoe series is both highly related to the core business and prominent on its own page, indicating strategic commitment and strong internal ability to develop it further.

Firefighter and rescue boots are more specialized and niche than the firm's mainstream range, but they still build on substantial existing protective-footwear knowledge, making retention more likely than exit.

A moulded insole is a natural extension of the firm's footwear platform and was highlighted on the home page, suggesting confidence that existing development and production resources can scale and refine it.
